bonds.analysis: For the 5-year investment horizon, a laddered maturity structure can be implemented to spread out the maturity dates across years. To adhere to the 'no more than 30% maturing in any single year' rule, we will allocate securities across multiple maturity buckets. We propose a portfolio consisting of the following allocation fractions: 25% in 1-year maturity, allocated to a 1-year Treasury bill; 20% in 2-year maturity, allocated to a 2-year government bond; 25% in 3-year maturity, allocated to a 3-year corporate bond with an investment-grade rating; 15% in 4-year maturity, allocated to a 4-year municipal bond; and 15% in 5-year maturity, allocated to a 5-year government agency bond. This configuration ensures that no more than 30% of the portfolio matures in any single year.
